# The directional condition from all active circuit selections

This note proves a smooth/transverse, sharp-center version of the directional
value formula. It does not assert that every mixed-integer depth minimizer
satisfies its extra regularity hypotheses. Its point is to retain the inner
optimization over ALL active balanced circuits rather than fixing one
arbitrary critical cap cover.

## 1. An abstract sharp max-min differentiation lemma

Let p range in an open subset of a finite-dimensional vector space. Let X
and A be compact sets, with X containing a neighborhood of x0 in R^d. Suppose
phi(p,x,a) is continuous, is continuously differentiable in (p,x) near
(p0,x0) uniformly over a in A, and is uniformly Lipschitz in p on the relevant
compact set. Put

    f(p,x)=min_(a in A) phi(p,x,a),
    V(p)=max_(x in X) f(p,x).

Assume x0 is the unique maximizer at p0 and is interior to X. Let A0 be the
compact active set where phi(p0,x0,a)=V(p0), and write

    q_a=grad_x phi(p0,x0,a),
    B_a(delta)=D_p phi(p0,x0,a)[delta].

Assume 0 lies in the INTERIOR of conv{q_a:a in A0} in R^d. Then, for every
direction delta, the one-sided directional derivative exists and is

    V'(p0;delta)=max_(h in R^d) min_(a in A0) [B_a(delta)+q_a.h].       (1)

Proof. The interior condition gives c>0 with
min_a q_a.h<=-2c|h|. Uniform differentiability of the active functions then
gives f(p0,x)<=V(p0)-c|x-x0| near x0. Uniqueness and compactness give a strict
gap away from that neighborhood. Uniform Lipschitz continuity in p implies
that every maximizing x_t at p0+t delta satisfies x_t=x0+O(t): compare its
value with f(p0+t delta,x0), and use the sharp linear drop.

For bounded h, uniform differentiability and compactness of A give uniformly

    f(p0+t delta,x0+t h)
      =V(p0)+t min_(a in A0)[B_a(delta)+q_a.h]+o(t).

For clarity, an upper bound follows by testing active a. For a lower bound,
choose minimizing a_t; every limit point is active, and uniform continuity
of the parameter derivatives gives the asserted expansion. Taking maximizing
h_t=(x_t-x0)/t, which are bounded, proves the upper bound in (1); testing any
fixed h proves the lower bound. The interior condition makes the right side
coercive from above, so its maximum is attained. This proves (1).

## 2. Exact balanced-circuit dual

For finite A0, elementary linear-programming duality rewrites (1) as

    min { sum_a theta_a B_a(delta):
          theta_a>=0, sum_a theta_a=1, sum_a theta_a q_a=0 }.          (2)

The feasible set is a nonempty compact polytope. Every vertex is supported
on at most d+1 active gradients, and a support-minimal vertex gives a positive
circuit. For compact A0 the same conclusion holds with probability measures
of zero q-moment; the optimum is attained and has a representative on at most
d+1 points. One can prove this by taking the convex hull of the compact set
{(q_a,B_a(delta))}; the lowest point above q=0 lies on a supporting hyperplane,
and Caratheodory within that face gives at most d+1 support points.

Thus the value derivative takes the MINIMUM over balanced circuits. A
stationarity certificate for one convenient circuit does not replace this
minimum.

## 3. Application to a finite smooth cap family

For a fixed integer index z and a smooth fiber-body parameter p, consider
cap functions through (z,x):

    phi_zj(p,x)=mu_p{(w,xi):v_j.(w-z)+u_j.(xi-x)>=0}.

Assume all relevant cuts are transverse, and assume a finite family, or a
compact uniformly smooth family, represents the local depth function. The
latter is an explicit hypothesis; it is not claimed for arbitrary bodies.
If each u_j is unit, let S_zj be the total section (d-1)-measure. Then

    q_zj=-S_zj u_j,
    B_zj(delta)=the ordinary body-shape derivative of that cap mass.

A cap active at an interior center has S_zj>0. The balanced probabilities in
(2) obey sum theta_j S_zj u_j=0. In terms of a positive circuit
sum rho_j u_j=0, sum rho_j=1, they are

    theta_j=(rho_j/S_zj)/(sum_l rho_l/S_zl).

The corresponding circuit derivative is exactly

    L_z,rho(delta)
       =[sum_j rho_j B_zj(delta)/S_zj]/[sum_j rho_j/S_zj].            (3)

Consequently the unnormalized restricted maximum derivative is the minimum
of (3) over all active circuits. The reciprocal section areas, rather than
unweighted circuit coefficients, are required.

## 4. Several deepest fibers and the robust transversal condition

Suppose every globally deepest fiber has one interior maximizer satisfying
the hypotheses above. Suppose every other fiber has a strict depth gap.
Write M(p) for the smooth total mass and beta for the original normalized
maximum. Only the deepest fibers contribute to its directional derivative:

    beta'(delta)=(1/M) max_(z deepest) min_(rho active at z)
                     [L_z,rho(delta)-beta M'(delta)].              (4)

Let Gamma_z be the compact convex set of linear functionals obtained by
allowing every balanced probability theta in (2) and subtracting beta M'.
For a finite cap family it is a linear image of a compact polytope. Formula
(4) is equivalently

    beta'(delta)=(1/M) max_z min_(g in Gamma_z) g(delta).

At a true local minimum this quantity must be nonnegative for every
admissible delta. If the body parameters range over an open set, so every
signed direction is allowed, an equivalent necessary condition is

    FOR EVERY selection g_z in Gamma_z, one has
                  0 in conv{g_z : z deepest}.                      (5)

Indeed a failed convex-hull inclusion is strictly separated by a direction
on which all selected g_z are negative, making (4) negative. Conversely,
if (4) is negative, choose a minimizing g_z for each z; their convex hull
is strictly separated from zero by that direction. This proves equivalence.
With an admissible cone D, replace the convex-hull condition by absence of
a direction delta in D strictly negative on all selected functionals.

Condition (5) quantifies over EVERY rainbow selection of active circuit
functionals. It is materially stronger than existence of a normalized stress
for one selected cover. It is still a necessary variational condition, not a
numerical mixed-integer Grünbaum inequality.

## 5. A strong consequence when only one fiber is deepest

Under the same open-parameter and smooth/sharp hypotheses, if there is only
one deepest fiber then

    Gamma_z={0}.

In other words, EVERY balanced active circuit, not merely one chosen circuit,
has exactly the volume-normalized objective derivative:

    L_z,rho(delta)=beta M'(delta) for every signed direction delta.

This follows immediately from (5), or by applying (4) to both delta and
-delta. This is an equality of linear functionals on the full parameter
space. For constrained parameters it instead gives
L_z,rho-beta M' in the dual of the admissible cone for every active circuit.

## 6. Exact diagnostic on the A=0 obstruction

For the family in candidate e7fde0ecffd41ff1, the central
fiber is uniquely deepest. At equal outer scales, vertex-direction caps can
independently choose any outer fiber to include. The A=0 selection includes
three different outer fibers and gives zero first-order change along the
radius variation (1-t,1,1+t). The alternative circuit selecting the shrinking
outer fiber for all three caps gives unnormalized derivative -2a, while
M'=0. Therefore beta'=-2a/(4a)=-1/2, exactly matching

    beta(t)=(13/9-2t+t^2)/(4+2t^2).

So the alternative-circuit condition detects the strict descent that the
single balanced A=0 stress misses. This diagnostic does not establish the
smooth representation assumptions for arbitrary cap families; the exact
explicit depth formula independently verifies it in this example.
